chunks: And from him, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Zurarah, who said:

I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: 'Indeed, among the matters are those that are restricted (mudayyiqah) and those that are expanded (mawsu'ah). And indeed, time is of two types: Prayer is among those that are expanded, so sometimes the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) would hasten it and sometimes delay it, except for the Friday Prayer, for indeed the Friday Prayer is among the restricted matters; it has only one time, when the sun passes its zenith (Zawal). And the time of the Asr prayer on Friday is the time of Dhuhr in the other days.'

key_terms.حِينَ تَزُولُ: When the sun passes its zenith (Zawal)

ai.seo_question: What is the specific timing rule for Friday Prayer and Asr on Friday according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) distinguishes between prayers with flexible timing (mawsu'ah) and those with strict, fixed timing (mudayyiqah), noting that while most prayers allow for hastening or delaying, Friday Prayer is strictly fixed to the time of Zawal. He further clarifies that the Asr prayer on Friday coincides with the Dhuhr time of other days, a nuance that complements reports on the specific merits of the night and day of Jumu'ah. This hadith underscores the jurisprudential precision in Shia fiqh regarding the unique temporal status of Jumu'ah prayers compared to daily obligations.
